claim: For every integer \(n\ge3\), let \(\operatorname{Cr}_n=K_{n,n}-\{a_i b_i:1\le i\le n\}\). The previously published parity formula is \(\gamma_{\mathrm{StR}}(\operatorname{Cr}_n)=n+1\) for odd \(n\) and \(n+2\) for even \(n\). The minimum strong Roman dominating functions admit a complete classification. If \(n=2m+1\), there are exactly \(n\) minimum functions: for one index \(k\), \(f(a_k)=f(b_k)=m+1\) and every other label is zero. If \(n=2m\), every minimum function is in exactly one of five support families: a common singleton; a two-vertex support on one side and its common singleton on the other, in either orientation; two two-vertex supports meeting in exactly one index; or identical two-vertex supports with the strong index chosen independently on the two sides. Their total number is exactly \(n(n^2+n-1)\). Thus the published minimum value has a rigid odd-order optimum space but a cubic-size even-order optimum space.
integrity: The proof derives an exact fixed-zero-support optimization before extracting equality cases. A standalone checker exhaustively verifies all labelings for \(n=3,4,5\) and independently scans support parameters through \(n=50\). Finite checks support but do not replace the infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The scalar strong Roman domination number of crown graphs is already published; the assessed contribution is only the complete classification and exact count of minimum functions. No full nonminimum weight enumerator is claimed, and an obscure poorly indexed equivalent classification remains a bibliographic risk.
title: All minimum strong Roman dominating functions of crown graphs
